questions.question: How many Lakhs are equal to 1 Million in the International System of Numeration?
questions.hint_modal: Recall core principles from Chapter 1: 1 Million = 1,000,000. In the Indian System, 10 Lakhs = 10 *...

solution_key.part2_method: Apply exact mathematical formula or logical deduction step
solution_key.part3_conclusion: 1 Million = 1,000,000. In the Indian System, 10 Lakhs = 10 * 100,000 = 1,000,000. Thus, 1 Million equals 10 Lakhs.

solution_key.part3_conclusion: 1 Crore = 1,00,00,000, which has 7 zeros following 1, so it is written as 10^7.

questions.question: If natural numbers 1, 2, 3, ... are written sequentially (123456789101112...), determine the exact digit present at position 100.
questions.hint_modal: Recall core principles from Chapter 1: Single-digit numbers 1-9 occupy 9 positions. Remaining posit...

solution_key.part2_method: Apply exact mathematical formula or logical deduction step
solution_key.part3_conclusion: Single-digit numbers 1-9 occupy 9 positions. Remaining positions needed = 100 - 9 = 91 positions. Two-digit numbers occupy 2 positions each: 91 / 2 = 45 complete numbers with a remainder of 1 position. The 45th two-digit number after 9 is 9 + 45 = 54. The next two-digit number is 55. The 1st digit of 55 is '5', which sits at the 100th digit position.

hotspots.title: Indian Place Value System
hotspots.popover_content: Lakh = 10^5, Crore = 10^7. Commas placed after 3 digits from right, then every 2 digits.

hotspots.title: International Place Value System
hotspots.popover_content: Million = 10^6, Billion = 10^9. Commas placed every 3 digits. 1 Crore = 10 Millions.

hotspots.title: Factor Shortcuts (x5 and x25)
hotspots.popover_content: N * 5 = (N / 2) * 10. N * 25 = (N / 4) * 100. Halve and scale by 10, or quarter and scale by 100.

hotspots.title: Sequential Digit Position Analytics
hotspots.popover_content: Digits 1-9 take 9 positions; 10-99 take 180 positions. Finding position 100 yields digit 5.
